doc.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023

title: Teaching as a two-way street; Makoto Ozone's arrival in Boston
summary: Wilson had free rein to teach and describes nurturing talent, especially Makoto Ozone's first night in Boston.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Speaking of that, when you started there did you have free reign to establish a teaching method of your own pedagogy, whatever it was, was it up to you to decide?
Good. Well I think that’s the best a young person could hope for is to land with a person who just got off the road and who knew what the life was like and what was needed from musicians.
Um hum. Teaching is a two-way street. Teaching is a two-way street. You know?

A guy comes into your office and you say, “Well let’s play a tune.” And you know pretty much where he’s at when within about 30 seconds. And you can recognize budding talent at all levels. I mean the level is huge. So once you’ve — I mean there’s the one who hasn’t a musical bone in his or her body but there are those and you kind of gently try to aim them in another direction. Then you have Makoto Ozone and Kirill Gerstein coming in at the age of twelve and you go oh my God is that unbelievable. And then you try to create an environment to have that person nurture his or her talent and that’s what I did with Makoto Ozone who came in when he was twenty from — on an airplane from Japan knowing 50 English words and having a ticket for his first night in Boston at the Holiday Inn in Cambridge which is just about two miles from the airport. This was late at night and the cab driver took him 45 miles away to another Holiday Inn in Northbridge. Yeah. And left him there. I mean you could imagine. Boy. So the manager at the Holiday Inn in Northbridge recognized what had happened. Here’s a guy who barely has no English, or 50 words is what he used to say. And there was a room which had a broken key or something like that and they let him stay free in that room overnight and then they arranged some sort of a ride back to Berklee. Son of a bitch, right? Sorry.
